title: Turn a percent ± MOE into a range of counts
subtitle: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error  · 1 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **1 of the official questions in Inference from sample statistics and margin of error  are this one** — 0 Easy, 1 Medium, 0 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The estimate and margin of error are both given as percents, but the population is a stated total count.
- The question asks for a plausible NUMBER of items or people (often labeled with a variable), and the choices are numeric ranges or inequalities on that count.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find the low and high percents: estimate − MOE and estimate + MOE.
- 2) Multiply each by the population total to get a count interval.
- 3) Choose the value or inequality that falls inside that count interval.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Optional: type low%*N and high%*N to get both endpoints.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You add the MOE percent as a raw count (for example, ±2 items instead of ±2% of the total).
You multiply by the sample size instead of the population.
Or you use only the point estimate and pick a choice that lies just outside the true interval.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
